heading: Liji 10 · Nei Ze 內則 · The Pattern Of The Family · Nei Ze I.1 … Nei Ze I.10

items.text: Rise at first cockcrow, wash and dress, then go to your parents; ask if they are warm or cold, ill or pained, and help them move and wash.
items.quote: ask if their clothes are (too) warm or (too) cold, whether they are ill or pained

items.text: Serve your parents-in-law as you served your own parents, tending to their comfort and needs.
items.quote: (Sons') wives should serve their parents-in-law as they served their own.

items.text: At daybreak, go to your parents, pay your respects, and ask what they will eat and drink; if they have not eaten, remain to help.
items.quote: as soon as it is daybreak, they should (go to) pay their respects (to their parents) and ask what they will eat and drink

items.text: When your parents have not eaten, assist your elder siblings in preparing what is needed.
items.quote: if they have not eaten, they will (remain to) assist their elder (brothers and sisters) and see what has been prepared.

items.text: If you hold official appointment, still pay your father respects at dawn and evening though you live apart.
items.quote: at the dawn, the son will pay his respects... At sundown, the son will pay his evening visit

items.text: When your parents wish to sit or lie down, carry their mats and stool, ask how to place them, and help them settle.
items.quote: When the parents wish to sit (anywhere), the sons and their wives should carry their mats, and ask in what direction they shall lay them.

items.text: Do not move or use your parents' clothes, mats, pillows, stools, or vessels, except what remains for you.
items.quote: should not move the clothes, coverlets, fine mats, or undermats, pillows, and stools of their parents

items.text: At meals when both parents are alive, encourage them to eat, then eat what is left.
items.quote: the (eldest) son and his wife will encourage them to eat everything, and what is left after all, they will themselves eat

items.text: When your father is dead, wait upon your mother at her meals.
items.quote: When the father is dead, and the mother still alive, the eldest son should wait upon her at her meals

heading: Liji 10 · Nei Ze 內則 · The Pattern Of The Family · Nei Ze I.19 … Nei Ze I.30

items.text: Ask leave from your parents-in-law before doing anything or withdrawing to your own apartment.
items.quote: No daughter-in-law, without being told to go to her own apartment, should venture to withdraw. Whatever she is about to do, she should ask leave from them.

items.text: Have no private goods, animals, or vessels; neither you nor your wife may borrow from or give to another person.
items.quote: A son and his wife should have no private goods, nor animals, nor vessels; they should not presume to borrow from, or give anything to, another person.

items.text: When given any food, dress, cloth, or ornament, offer it to your parents-in-law; if they return it, lay it by for their use and ask leave before giving it to your cousins.
items.quote: she should receive and offer it to her parents-in-law... If she want to give it to some of her own cousins, she must ask leave

items.text: Do reverent service to the family's representative chief and his wife; do not enter his house with any display of your wealth or rank.
items.quote: should do reverent service to the son, who is the representative chief of the family and his wife... not enter his house with demonstrations of wealth and dignity.

items.text: If you receive vessels, robes, carriages or horses, offer the best to the chief of the clan, and use only what is inferior yourself.
items.quote: he must offer the best of them (to his chief), and then use those that are inferior to this himself.

items.text: Prepare two sacrificial victims, present the better to the chief, and with your wife assist reverently at his ancestral sacrifice before offering your own.
items.quote: prepare two victims, and present the better of them to his chief. He and his wife should together... reverently assist at his sacrifice in the ancestral temple.
items.conflict: Ancestral offerings and temple sacrifice are not commanded; Deut 18:10-12 forbids such practices.

heading: Liji 10 · Nei Ze 內則 · The Pattern Of The Family · Nei Ze I.31 … Nei Ze II.2

items.text: Nourish your aged parents: gladden their hearts, do not oppose their wishes, make their bedchamber and whole house comfortable, and with a true heart supply their food and drink throughout your life.
items.quote: A filial son, in nourishing his aged, (seeks to) make their hearts glad, and not to go against their wishes; to promote their comfort in their bed-chambers and the whole house; and with leal heart to supply them with their food and drink

items.text: Love what your parents loved and reverence what they reverenced, even to their dogs and horses, and much more the people they valued.
items.quote: Thus what his parents loved he will love, and what they reverenced he will reverence. He will do so even in regard to all their dogs and horses, and how much more in regard to the men (whom they valued)!

items.text: After your parents turn sixty, keep their coffin and funeral items ready, checked yearly at sixty, each season at seventy, monthly at eighty, and daily at ninety.
items.quote: After sixty (the coffin and other things for the funeral) were seen to be in readiness (once) a year; after seventy, once a season; after eighty, once a month; and after ninety, they were every day kept in good repair.

heading: Liji 10 · Nei Ze 內則 · The Pattern Of The Family · Nei Ze II.33 … Nei Ze II.37

items.text: When going out, coming in, or going to eat, follow your elders and yield to them.
items.quote: when going out or coming in at a gate or door, and going to their mats to eat and drink, they were required to follow their elders

items.text: Practice filial piety: honor, obey, and serve your parents diligently.
items.quote: attended sedulously to filial and fraternal duties

items.text: Practice fraternal duty: respect and defer to your elder siblings.
items.quote: attended sedulously to filial and fraternal duties

items.text: Be docile and obedient; learn woman's work and household duties.
items.quote: to be docile and obedient, to handle the hempen fibres, to deal with the cocoons, to weave silks and form fillets

items.text: Attend to the business proper to a man: provide for your household and manage outside affairs.
items.quote: At thirty, he had a wife, and began to attend to the business proper to a man.

items.text: Do not go to a man without betrothal rites; otherwise you become his concubine, not his wife.
items.quote: If there were the betrothal rites, she became a wife; and if she went without these, a concubine.
items.conflict: Marriage is a covenant between one man and one woman; concubinage is adulterous (Gen 2:24)

heading: Liji 10 · Nei Ze 內則 · The Pattern Of The Family · Nei Ze I.11 … Nei Ze I.18

items.text: Sons and their wives: obey your parents' orders immediately and reverently; if given food or clothes you dislike, accept them; if your task is given to another, cooperate and redo if needed.
items.quote: when ordered to do anything, should immediately respond and reverently proceed to do it... if (their parents) give them anything to eat or drink, which they do not like, they will notwithstanding taste it

items.text: In your parents' presence, abstain from belching, sneezing, coughing, yawning, stretching, standing on one foot, leaning, looking askance, spitting, sniveling, scratching, or exposing your body; do not display the inside of your private dress; do not allow their spittle or snivel to be seen; ask leave to rinse dirt from caps or girdles, wash clothes, and stitch rents.
items.quote: should not presume to eructate, sneeze, or cough... They should not allow the spittle or snivel of their parents to be seen.

items.text: Every five days prepare warm water and ask them to bathe; every three days water to wash their heads; if their faces or feet are dirty, prepare appropriate water.
items.quote: Every five days they should prepare tepid water, and ask them to take a bath, and every three days prepare water for them to wash their heads.

items.text: Men and women: do not discuss inside or outside matters, hand vessels except at sacrifices and funerals, share wells, baths, mats, or clothing, or borrow from one another; men do not whistle or point indoors; women cover their faces outdoors and keep to the left; use a light when moving at night.
items.quote: The men should not speak of what belongs to the inside, nor the women of what belongs to the outside... they should not go to the same well, nor to the same bathing-house.

items.text: Instruct unfilial sons and daughters-in-law; if they refuse instruction, be angry; if anger fails, expel them, but do not publicly shame them.
items.quote: If they will not receive instruction, they should then be angry with them. If that anger do no good, they can then drive out the son, and send the wife away, yet not publicly showing why.
items.conflict: Parental discipline should be corrective, not disowning (Eph 6:4); expulsion and sending away a wife is not a church discipline pattern.

items.text: If a parent errs, admonish gently; if not heeded, be more reverent; if beaten, do not resent but remain more reverent.
items.quote: the son should with bated breath, and bland aspect, and gentle voice, admonish him... if the parent be angry and beat him till the blood flows, he should not presume to be angry and resentful.
items.conflict: Honoring parents does not require accepting abusive beating (Col 3:21; 1 Tim 5:8).

items.text: After your parents' death, do not let your regard for their beloved son or grandson decay.
items.quote: their sons should after their death, not allow their regard for him to decay so long as they live.

items.text: Do not elevate the concubine you prefer above the one your parents loved; continue honoring her after their death.
items.quote: he should not dare to make this one equal to the former whom his parents love, in dress, or food, or the duties... nor should he lessen his attentions to her after their death.
items.conflict: Concubinage is outside God's design for marriage (Gen 2:24; 1 Tim 3:2).

items.text: If your parents dislike your wife, divorce her; if they approve, keep her as your wife all her life.
items.quote: If he very much approves of his wife, and his parents do not like her, he should divorce her. If he do not approve of his wife, and his parents say, 'she serves us well,' he should behave to her in all respects as his wife.
items.conflict: Marriage is a covenant not subject to parents' arbitrary dissolution (Matt 19:6).

items.text: When inclined to do good, consider that it will transmit your parents' good name; when inclined to evil, consider that it will disgrace them, and refrain.
items.quote: when a son is inclined to do what is good, he should think that he will thereby transmit the good name of his parents... when he is inclined to do what is not good, he should think that he will thereby bring disgrace on the name of his parents.

items.text: When your father-in-law is dead, ask your mother-in-law for directions in everything regarding sacrifices and receiving guests.
items.quote: the wife of the eldest son, on all occasions of sacrificing and receiving guests, must ask her directions in everything.

items.text: If you are a younger daughter-in-law, ask the eldest brother's wife for directions, and do not consider yourself her equal: do not walk side by side, give orders, or sit as she does.
items.quote: the other sons' wives must ask directions from her... they should not presume to consider themselves on an equality with the other; walking side by side with her, or giving their orders in the same way, or sitting in the same position as she.

heading: Liji 10 · Nei Ze 內則 · The Pattern Of The Family · Nei Ze II.18 … Nei Ze II.32

items.text: At three months, present your son to his father.
items.quote: On that day the wife with the son appeared before the father.

items.text: Teach your child to follow the right way.
items.quote: Reverently (teach him to) follow the right way.

items.text: Name your son at three months, taking his right hand and speaking gently and joyfully.
items.quote: He then took hold of the right hand of his son, and named him with the smile and voice of a child.

items.text: Do not give your son a name that is a day, month, state, or hidden ailment, nor the name of the ruler's heir.
items.quote: In naming a son, the name should not be that of a day or a month or of any state, or of any hidden ailment.

items.text: Receive and name your grandson when his father is alive.
items.quote: In all cases though the father is alive, the grandson is presented to the grandfather, who also names him.

items.text: Nourish your child yourself.
items.quote: The wife of an ordinary officer nourished her child herself.

items.text: Teach a boy to answer boldly and clearly, a girl submissively and low.
items.quote: a boy (was taught to) respond boldly and clearly; a girl, submissively and low

items.text: During your wife's confinement, separate from her room and ask after her daily.
items.quote: the husband left his bed-chamber, and occupied a common apartment

items.text: On the birth of your child, entertain your parents-in-law as at your first reception.
items.quote: a feast was celebrated with the ceremonies of that with which a wife first entertains her parents-in-law.

items.text: When your child is three months old, present yourself and the child to the wife proper, as at your first entrance.
items.quote: appeared in the inner chamber (belonging to the wife proper). There she was received with the ceremonies of her first entrance into the harem.

heading: Liji 10 · Nei Ze 內則 · The Pattern Of The Family · Nei Ze II.3 … Nei Ze II.17

items.text: Do not use your husband's stands, boxes, or bathing-house; keep your belongings separate from his.
items.quote: The wife did not presume to hang up anything on the pegs or stand of her husband; nor to put anything in his boxes or satchels; nor to share his bathing-house.

items.text: When your husband has gone out, put away his pillow and mats in their proper places.
items.quote: When her husband had gone out (from their apartment), she put his pillow in its case, rolled up his upper and under mats, put them in their covers, and laid them away in their proper receptacles.

items.text: Serve elders and superiors; let the young serve the old and the low serve the noble.
items.quote: The young served the old; the low served the noble;—also in this way.

items.text: As the men occupy the exterior and the women the interior, do not cross into the other's domain.
items.quote: The men did not enter the interior; the women did not come out into the exterior.

items.text: As a concubine, be with your husband once every five days until you are fifty.
items.quote: though a concubine were old, until she had completed her fiftieth year, it was the rule that she should be with the husband (once) in five days.
items.conflict: Polygamy/concubinage is contrary to God's design for marriage (Gen. 2:24; Matt. 19:5); a wife is to be one.

items.text: As a concubine, defer to the wife: in dress and diet come after her, and do not stay the whole night if she is absent.
items.quote: Even a favourite concubine was required in dress and diet to come after her superior. If the wife were not with the husband, a concubine waiting on him, would not venture to remain the whole night.
items.conflict: Secondary wives and ranking of women undermine the one-flesh union of a single husband and wife (Eph. 5:31).

items.text: During her confinement and after the birth, send twice a day to ask about her; fast and do not enter her side apartment.
items.quote: her husband sent twice a day to ask for her... When the child was born, the husband again sent twice a day to inquire for her.

items.text: During your confinement, do not presume to see your husband; let your governess dress and answer him.
items.quote: she did not presume to see him, but made her governess dress herself and reply to him.

items.text: When a son and heir is born, arrange a feast and have the tortoise-shell consulted to choose a man to carry him, shoot arrows to heaven, earth, and the four quarters, and consult again for a nurse.
items.quote: On the third day the tortoise-shell was consulted for a good man to carry the child... The master of the archers... shot towards heaven, earth, and the four cardinal points.
items.conflict: Divination by tortoise-shell is forbidden (Deut. 18:10-12); trust God's providence for your child.
